Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

SPECIFICATION FOR 

SCISSORS, McINDOE'S, FOR 

PLASTIC SURGERY 

0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard was adoptt d by the Indian Standards Insti- 
tution on 21 September 1967, after the draft finali/ed by the Suri^^ical 
Instruments Sectional Committee! had been approved by the Consumer 
Products Division Council. 

0,2 The formulation of Indian Standards on stn^ical instruments 
has been taken up on tlic recommendations of the Advisory Conunittee 
for Development of Suririral Instruments, Equipment arul Appliances 
of the Government of India. 

0.3 This Indian Standard is one of a scries on surgical instiumenls. 
Other standards published so far in the: scries appear on page 10. 

0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement 
of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculat- 
ed, expressing the result of a test, shiill b(^ loundecl ofT in accordance 
with IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant ])laces letaincd in the 
rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in 
this standard. 



1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard covers the requircmc nts for the following McIndoc*s 
scissors for plastic surgery: 

a) Dissecting, triangular blad( s, blunt points, sliaight, and cm vcd 
on flat; 

b) Straight, finc^ sharp points; and 

c) Curved on flat. 



*Uulea for rounding off numerical valuen ( revised), 

3 



IS : 4281 . 1967 

2. MATERIALS 

2.1 Scissors shall be made of stainless steel conforming to Designation 
30Crl3 of Schedule V of IS : 1570-1961* or to the following com- 
position: 

Percent 

Carbon O'SS to 0-45 

Silicon 0-10 to 0*70 

Manganese 0*30 to 0*70 

Nickel VOQ.Max 

Chromium 1200 to 1400 

2.2 Screws shall be made of stainless steel cither the same as used for 
the instrument or conforming to Designation 22Crl3S28 of Schedule V 
of IS: 1570-1961*. 

3. SHAPE AND DIMENSIONS 

3.1 Scissors shall conform generally to the shape and dimensions shown 
in Fig. 1, 2 and 3. 

3.2 Screw — Screw used shall be a slotted cheese head pattern as shown 
in Fig. 4 on P 8. The profile of the screw thread shall conform to 
IS : 1362-1962t. The thread shall be of such length as to allow sufficient 
shank for proper bearing surface and to adequately secure component 
parts of the scissors. Screw shall retain proper position after setting 
without binding or loosening during use and shall be flush with the 
surface of the blades. 

3.3 Finger Loop — Finger loop shall be properly shaped and the size 
shall conform to Size No. 2 of 12 of Section 5 of IS : 3642-1966$. 

4. WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 

4.1 Scissors shall be symmetrical and well-balanced. 

4.2 The blades along their length and the tips shall coincide and shall 
not override, when the scissors are fully closed. 

4.3 The blades shall open and close without stiffness and shall have a 
slight crossover action to give a continuous pinch and shall have no play 
at the joints.

4.4 Scissors shall he frrr froTii cracks, scams, burrs, flaws and other dc- 
fccis. Tile sill faces (>(" the scissors shall be passivatcd and iinishcd 
smooth and brii^ht. The irdg<^s shall be even and rounded except for

any feathrr. 

5. HARDNESS 

5»1 Scissors shall be evenly haidencd and tempered to 550 to 600 //K. 

6. TESTS 

6.1 Performance — I'he cutting edges from pinch to the tips shall cut 
wet tissue paper, tcascd-out cotton wool, fine haiis and frayed lint 
accurately and cleanly. 

6.2 Hardness ~ When tested on a hardness testing machine, the scissors 
shall have a Vicker's diamond pyramici hardness number as specified 
in 5.1. 

6.3 Flexibility — The flexibility shall be tested as given in 6.3.1 
and 6.3.2.

6.3.1 The finger loop of one arm of the scissors shall ])C lixcd at its 
equator in a vice, with the shank and tlic bhule pi ( jfctiiii^ above 
the vice. By the application of force at a point 75 mm above tiic vice 
the shank shall be d( fleeted at right angles to tin: plan<^ of the finger 
loop to a distance of 10 mm as measuied at the tip of tlie blade. On 
release of the force, no permanent set shall be (^b crved. 

6.3.2 The test shall be repeated on the same arm with tlie arm fixed 
in the vice near the joint so that 75 nun of the shank ( as nn asured fi om 
the upper surface of the vice jaws to tlie upper pole of the linger looj) ) 
proti'udes above the vice. The deilcrting for(^c shall be aj^plied at tlu* 
upper pole of the linger loop and shall ;i( t in a plane at ri,:;lit angU-s Lo 
the plane of the finger looj>. The shank shall be (h ih . ted by 5 nun as 
measured at the upper pole of the linger loo]). On relea e (-f the foice, 
no permanent set shall be observed.

7. MARKING 

7,1 Scissors shall be legibly and indelibly marked with the manufac- 
turer's name, initials or registered trade-nnuk and in addition with the 
words ' Stainless Steel \ 

7.1.1 The scissors may also be marked with the TSI Certification 
Mark.

8. PACKING 

8.1 Each pair ofscissors siiall be wrapped in moistuieproof polyethylene 
bag and packed in cartons in a manner that coming into contact with 
each other is avoided.
